Krier Foods’ rich heritage began in 1908 as a small farming company in Belgium, Wisconsin called The Belgium Cannery.
#### 1913
J.B Krier sells his interest in The Belgium Cannery and founds The Krier Preserving Company.
#### 1923
Due to the growing demand and success, a second canning plant is established in nearby Random Lake, Wisconsin.
#### 1942
The common stock is purchased, and the company transitions to being family-owned.

The Krier Preserving Company expands its vegetable canning operation to include a significant move into beverage processing.
#### 1966
Jolly Good soda line is added. The name is taken from an original vegetable label from the early years of the canning company.
#### 1972
The Krier Preserving Company purchases the Wisconsin Foods fruit packaging division in Sturgeon Bay, Wisconsin from Ward Foods of New York.
#### 1982
The Krier Preserving Company changes its name to Krier Foods due to the national consciousness regarding sodium and other preservatives.
#### 1988
Krier Foods sells their vegetable canning plants in Belgium and Random Lake to Lakeside Foods, Inc. of Manitowoc, Wisconsin. Krier continues to use a portion of the plant to operate as privately held company specializing in carbonated and non-carbonated beverage contract manufacturing.

Krier Foods becomes one of the early few beverage companies to fill pasteurized juices in single serve aluminum cans, furthering its relationship with nationally branded beverage companies.
#### 2018
Krier Foods acquires a brewer’s permit allowing it to manufacture alcoholic beverages.
